messages:
laura: Hey folks — seeing a pretty funky behavior in our Android sample app with Retrofit/OkHttp. If a coroutine times out and we cancel the Call, the socket doesn't close right away and threads pile up on older devices. Repro below, anyone seen this?

sam: Ugh yes, saw something similar a while back on Pixel 3/emulator. Is this with callTimeout vs readTimeout?

laura: It's with per-request coroutine timeout:
```kotlin
withTimeout(1500) {
  api.getBigResponse() // Retrofit suspend call
}
```
OkHttp client is configured with connectTimeout 10s, readTimeout 0 (no timeout), callTimeout 30s.

alex: Interesting. When you cancel the coroutine does Call.cancel() run?

laura: We cancel via coroutine cancellation which uses the OkHttp Coroutine adapter — yes that triggers Call.cancel(). The problem: connection socket -> FIN doesn't seem to send immediately on Android 9/10 emulators and the Dispatcher threads remain BUSY. Over time we hit thread pool exhaustion in tests.

mike: Do you have logs / thread dump?

laura: Pasted remote thread dump from repro run:
```
OkHttp ConnectionPool (idle=2)
Thread-139 RUNNABLE java.net.SocketInputStream.socketRead0(Native Method)
Thread-139 at java.net.SocketInputStream.read(SocketInputStream.java:...)
Thread-139 at okio.Okio$1.read(Okio.java:...)
Thread-139 at okio.AsyncTimeout$1.read(AsyncTimeout.java:...)
Thread-139 at okhttp3.internal.http2.Http2Connection$ReaderRunnable.execute(Http2Connection.java:...)
```
The sockets are stuck in read for a while after cancel.

sam: That looks like call.cancel did not interrupt the underlying socket read. On some Android builds the JVM's socket interrupt doesn't map to ASIO read interruption.

alex: Two possible axes: 1) callTimeout vs coroutine cancel handling 2) HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1 flow. Are you using HTTP/2 multiplexing?

laura: Yes HTTP/2 enabled. Repro toggling to force HTTP/1.1 stops the leak. So it seems HTTP/2 cancel path is involved.

mike: Workaround: set readTimeout to a small value or call dispatcher.executorService().shutdownNow() in test teardown? Not great for prod. Another option is proactively closing the socket via EventListener onCallFailed and call.connection()?.socket()?.close() but that's fragile.

alex: There's an open OkHttp bug about interrupting blocking reads on older Android kernels for HTTP/2 streams. IIRC that was tracked to AsyncTimeout#timedOut path not running when cancel races with frame reader.

laura: I tried forcing Call.timeout().cancel() on coroutine cancellation before Call.cancel() but still saw a window where reader stuck.

sam: Small repro snippet that may help debug:
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .callTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(30))
  .connectTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
  .build()
val retrofit = Retrofit.Builder()
  .client(client)
  .baseUrl("https://localhost:8443/")
  .addConverterFactory(MoshiConverterFactory.create())
  .build()
// coroutine
val job = launch { withTimeout(1500) { service.getLarge() } }
delay(2000)
// observe threads before/after
```

laura: I can attach a trimmed CI log. Right now I just want to capture the thread so someone from SDK parity/runtime team can look.

mike: I'll open an internal issue with stack traces + minimal repro. tagging @eng-runtime. For immediate DX workaround in onboarding docs we should note: "If you use coroutine cancellations on Android <=10 with HTTP/2, consider setting read timeout or forcing HTTP/1.1".

alex: Also test against latest OkHttp 5.x snapshot — they changed some HTTP/2 cancellation wiring. Worth validating.

laura: Cool. I'll try the 5.x snapshot and paste results here. If that fails I'll attach a distilled sample app under devex/sample-apps.

ci-bot: Build failed — device-tests (Android 9 emulator) — leak-detector: thread-pool-exhaustion. See logs: https://ci.internal/1234

mike: Thanks, ci-bot. Laura, can you drop the minimal app + instructions in a GH gist? I'll link the internal issue.

laura: Will do. Thanks for quick eyes. :heart:
